subject: Request: jurisdictional audit snapshots + attestation handshake
messages:
From: Peter Lang <peter.lang@novamed.com>
To: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.ai>
Cc: AuditOps <auditops@novamed.com>
Date: 2026-08-17T09:12:00Z
Subject: Jurisdictional audit snapshots + attestation request

Mina — thanks for taking this. Novamed's privacy/compliance team needs two things for our SOC 2 review: a) the ability to request jurisdictional 'slices' (EU/US) of admin activity and audit logs for specified time windows, and b) an attested manifest (signed) that lists included objects with checksums and an HMAC attestation for chain-of-custody.

Key asks: 
- Example manifest CSV/format you can provide (we need a sample row).
- Options for ad-hoc snapshots vs scheduled exports and delivery mechanisms (SFTP, signed URL, or direct S3 cross-account).
- How you handle PII redaction in exported records and whether we can request tenant-scoped scrubbing.

Attached an intake questionnaire (novamed_questionnaire_v2.pdf) with our preferred export window (2026-07-01 to 2026-07-31) for a test snapshot. Please advise lead time and any constraints.

Thanks,
Peter
Peter Lang
Sr. Compliance Manager, Novamed
attachments: novamed_questionnaire_v2.pdf (application/pdf)

From: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.ai>
To: Peter Lang <peter.lang@novamed.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>, Logan Wright <logan_wright@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-08-17T11:07:00Z
Subject: Re: Jurisdictional audit snapshots + attestation request

Hi Peter — thanks for the clear asks and for the questionnaire. Quick summary of what we can offer and a proposed handshake flow: 

1) Snapshot scope and jurisdictional slicing
- We can slice the admin/audit ledger by region using the request's region tag (US / EU / APAC) and timezone normalization. Exports are per-tenant and can be constrained by user/role filters you specify.

2) Export formats + manifest
- Primary formats: newline-delimited JSON (ndjson) for event records, and CSV manifest that lists object_key, start_ts, end_ts, record_count, md5_checksum, hmac_signature
- We'll attach a sample manifest row for your intake test. Sample file: sample-manifest-rows.csv (see attachment).

3) Delivery options
- SFTP push to your lockbox (preferred for regulated customers), cross-account S3 (pre-signed role assumption), or time-limited signed HTTPS URL. All deliveries can be wrapped in a signed manifest (HMAC with our key) and a SHA256 tree hash for large bundles.

4) PII redaction
- Two modes: full-raw (no redaction) for authenticated auditor workflows, or tenant-scoped scrub (replace PII fields with deterministic salts). We'll include redaction metadata in the manifest and row-level redaction flags.

5) Attestation
- We can provide an attestation bundle: signed manifest (RSA 2048), HMAC chain-of-custody stamps for each file, and a short statement of export parameters. If you require an independent timestamping authority, we can add a time-stamp token.

Next steps / timeline:
- If you confirm delivery mechanism (SFTP vs S3) and redaction mode, we can prepare a test snapshot for the July window within 48 business hours, and deliver a signed manifest within the same handoff.

I've looped in Kimberly to own the packaging and Logan for secure transport.

Regards,
Mina Haddad
Security & Compliance (Redwood Inference)
attachments: sample-manifest-rows.csv (text/csv)

From: AuditOps <auditops@novamed.com>
To: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.ai>
Cc: Peter Lang <peter.lang@novamed.com>
Date: 2026-08-18T15:26:00Z
Subject: Re: Jurisdictional audit snapshots + attestation request

Mina — thanks, that layout looks promising. A couple clarifying items from our ops side: 

- For the 'tenant-scoped scrub' option, can you provide deterministic salts so we can re-identify test rows if needed for internal QA?
- For manifests: do you include timezone-normalized start/end timestamps (UTC ISO) and a per-file SHA256 plus an HMAC computed over the manifest row?
- Delivery: we'll request SFTP for the test. Our lockbox details: sftp-novamed.redwood.lockbox (we'll send creds once handshake is complete).

Action: Please confirm the exact field names in the manifest and whether you can include a small sample bundle (1–2 MB) with the HMAC header so our crypto team can validate signatures.

— AuditOps (on behalf of Novamed)
attachments: none

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
To: AuditOps <auditops@novamed.com>, Peter Lang <peter.lang@novamed.com>
Cc: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.ai>, Logan Wright <logan_wright@redwood.ai>, Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-08-19T14:42:00Z
Subject: Re: Jurisdictional audit snapshots + attestation request

Peter / AuditOps — confirmed. We'll produce a 2 MB sample bundle (US jurisdiction slice, 2026-07-01 to 2026-07-31) with the following characteristics: 

- Format: ndjson payloads, CSV manifest with columns: object_key,start_utc,end_utc,record_count,sha256_hex,md5_hex,hmac_hex,redaction_mode
- HMAC: HMAC-SHA256 over the manifest row using a pre-shared key. We'll provide the HMAC header on the transfer and include a detached RSA signature for the manifest file.
- Redaction: deterministic salt (per-tenant salt) available to Novamed in a separate KMS-wrapped envelope if you request re-identification for validation only.
- Delivery: SFTP push to the lockbox you provide. We will generate and rotate an expiring client key and provide transport logs as part of the attested bundle.
- Timeline: sample bundle ready by EOD 2026-08-21. Production-grade snapshot scheduling and retention policies can be discussed after the sample validates.

I'll raise a short Jira (RFC-EXPORT-3421) to track packaging decisions and share the Drive folder with the sample when ready: https://drive.redwood.ai/drive/folders/1XyAttestSnapshot

Let us know if we should include a time-stamp token from DigiStamp for the manifest.

Best,
Kimberly Park
Director, Customer Security Ops (Redwood Inference)
attachments: packaging-checklist.txt (text/plain)
